title: Acoustic Levitation
subject: Science
source: NYSED 2026 Grade 8 ILS Released Items, Questions 6-9
directions: Base your answers to questions 6 through 9 on the information below and on your knowledge of science.

intro.html: An acoustic levitator makes objects hover in the air between two small groups of speakers using sound waves. One group of speakers is above the hovering objects and the other group is below. When the sound waves produced by both groups of speakers have the same frequency, the waves combine and form quiet and loud areas. Small beads or drops of liquid put into the space between the speakers will be suspended in the quiet areas. The diagram below shows an acoustic levitator. The model below shows the quiet and loud areas between the two groups of speakers and the location of the suspended beads.

amplification.html: The speakers in the acoustic levitator are powered by electricity. The energy of the sound waves produced by the speakers is controlled with an amplifier. A section of an air pressure wave at a low amplification is shown below, drawn to scale.

amplification.caption: Low Amplification Wave
amplification.alt: A smooth wave line in a box with two rounded crests and one trough between them.

density.html: Different substances can be suspended in the acoustic levitator. The graph below shows the amount of peak-to-peak voltage (measurement similar to energy) required to suspend samples of equal-volume substances having different densities. The range is indicated for each data point.

density.caption:
Relationship Between Sample Density and
Peak-to-Peak Voltage of an Acoustic Levitator
density.alt: Graph with Peak-to-Peak Voltage (V) from 9 to 17 on the horizontal axis and Levitating Sample Density (g/cm3) from 0 to 2.5 on the vertical axis. Each of four labeled data points has a horizontal bar showing its range. Isopropyl alcohol is at about 9.9 volts and a density of about 0.8. Water is at about 11 volts and a density of 1. Sugar is at about 12.7 volts and a density of 1.5. Fused silica (Pure glass) is at about 15.8 volts and a density of about 2.2.

items.stem: Although acoustic levitation has many practical applications on Earth, it is not practical in space. Explain why the use of acoustic levitation, such as the one described using speakers, is not possible in outer space. [1]
rubric: Credit: The explanation implies that sound needs a medium through which to travel. This response is sufficient for credit.

Exemplary response: Sound needs a medium to travel, and space is a vacuum. OR A sound wave cannot travel in space since a medium is needed for it to move. OR Without the air/gas/air pressure/matter present on Earth, sound can not travel. OR Sound is a mechanical wave. OR other valid response

No credit: The explanation inaccurately specifies the medium needed for sound to travel as oxygen only. It also incorrectly describes the effect of gravity on sound transmission and incorrectly implies the existence of sound in space. This response is insufficient for credit due to an incorrect explanation.
No credit: The explanation does not address why sound cannot travel in space. This response is insufficient for credit due to an incomplete explanation.
items.exemplar: Sound needs a medium to travel, and space is a vacuum.
